annotations.title: List the site’s categories and tags

description: Returns the categories and tags THIS site already uses, with the exact names create-content and update-content expect. Those tools take terms by NAME, and a name typed from memory does not match one that exists — "New Features" and "New features" are two different categories, and the second one gets created. Read this first and reuse what is here. `field` on each group is the input field it maps to (`categories`, `tags`), `count` is how many published items already carry the term, and `total` says how many exist when the list is capped — narrow it with `search` rather than assuming you have seen them all. `notSettable` names public taxonomies this content type has that the write tools do NOT touch: they exist on the site, and nothing here can put a page in one.

post_type.description: Which content type’s taxonomies to list. Defaults to "post".

search.description: Only terms whose name contains this. Use it on a site with hundreds.

name: agentimus-read-terms

notSettable.description: Public taxonomies this content type has that the write tools cannot set. ⛔ Never tell an owner a page was filed in one of these.

postType.description: The content type these groups belong to.

canCreate.description: Whether the connected user may create a NEW term here. FALSE means an unknown name will be REFUSED, not quietly added — send names from this list.

field.description: The create-content / update-content input field for this group: "categories" or "tags".

hierarchical.description: TRUE when terms can have parents (categories do; tags do not).

description.description: Its description as stored, empty when it has none. update-term replaces it, so start from this.

name.description: Send this string, exactly as it appears here.

parent.description: 0 when top-level; only meaningful on a hierarchical group.

total.description: How many terms exist. Larger than the list below means the list was capped.
